title: Roles: product owner, team coach, developer and tester
blurb: Apply the guidance for the four delivery-level roles and choose who in a people list fits product owner, team coach, developer and tester.
question: At Callowmere University, which person is best suited to be product owner for the web team: the head of the web team, or the senior digital product manager who has managed its backlog for two years?

teach.h: Four roles inside each delivery team
teach.body: Every delivery team has the same make-up. The product owner (PO), a version of the team manager role, owns the team's product backlog and delivers agreed work within tolerances. The team coach helps one or two teams self-manage and improve. Developers design, build and maintain the product increments. Testers make sure the products meet their quality and acceptance criteria and the team's Definition of Done.

head: Role
Key duties
People-list clue
rows: Owns product backlog; writes and maintains user stories; agrees work with the PM
Has written and prioritized a team's stories
Self-management, trust, conflict, communication; facilitates team workshops
Designs, builds and maintains increments; solves technical issues
Builds, configures or designs the product
Designs, runs, possibly automates tests; checks criteria and DoD

teach.h: Product owner or chief product owner?
The product owner keeps the team aligned
teach.body: The PO prepares and maintains the product backlog and user stories and keeps them aligned with the project backlog, the continued business justification principle and the project tolerances. The PO agrees work package descriptions with the PM, delivers them within the agreed tolerances, works closely with the CPO and acts as a servant leader for the team. The PO does not prioritize across teams.

The team coach works closely with one or two specific teams to raise their effectiveness: helping them self-manage, building trust and accountability, refining processes, resolving conflicts and improving communication. The coach balances self-management with PRINCE2 Agile principles and tolerances, helps write user stories and facilitates team workshops such as team planning and retrospectives. A Scrum master fits this role well.

root.label: Team member in the people list

teach.caption: A line manager or head of department is not automatically the PO: look for who actually owns the backlog.

teach.body: Sasha Ellery has written and prioritized the app team's user stories for three years: product owner. Owen Thackeray, the Scrum master who facilitates sprint events and retrospectives, is the team coach. Hollie Brennan writes automated tests and checks stories against acceptance criteria: tester. The other app engineers are developers. Matteo Ricci, who sets direction across all digital channels, is the CPO rather than a team PO, and Priyanka Desai, who coaches leaders, is the agile coach.

teach.text: Near misses: a Scrum master is a team coach, not an agile coach. The head of a team who line-manages people is not automatically the product owner. An analyst who measures impact fits tester better than developer. A partly done story is not done: the tester checks against the DoD.

items: PO: version of the team manager; owns one team's product backlog; agrees work with the PM.
Team coach: one or two teams; self-management, conflict, communication; facilitates team workshops.
Developer: designs, builds and maintains increments; solves technical problems.
Tester: designs, runs and may automate tests; checks against criteria and the team DoD.
Pick people by what they actually do now, not by seniority.

summary: You can now apply the guidance for the product owner, team coach, developer and tester, and choose the best person for each from a people list. You can also separate the PO from the CPO and the team coach from the agile coach.

A.q: Callowmere University needs a product owner for the web team that will build the Student Support Hub. Which person is best suited to the role?
options: Daniel Ferreira, head of the web team
Rebecca Lyle, who has managed the team's backlog
Chloe Hartley, Scrum master for the web team
Dr Kwame Mensah, director of student wellbeing
A.why: The PO prepares and maintains the product backlog and user stories for one team (Table 7.2). Rebecca has managed the web team's backlog for two years.

whyNot.0: Being head of the team is a line management role; the PO is chosen for backlog ownership.
whyNot.2: A Scrum master fits the team coach role.
whyNot.3: Kwame represents the users across the project and fits the chief product owner role.

A.q: Larkspur Rail needs a team coach for the in-house app team. Which person is best suited to the role?
options: Owen Thackeray, who facilitates the app team's sprints
Priyanka Desai, who has coached senior managers
Sasha Ellery, who writes the app team's user stories
Hollie Brennan, who writes the team's automated tests
A.why: The team coach works closely with one or two teams, facilitates team workshops and helps them self-manage; a Scrum master fits the role (Table 7.2).

whyNot.1: Coaching leaders and departments across the organization fits the agile coach.
whyNot.2: Writing and prioritizing the team's stories fits the product owner.
whyNot.3: Writing tests and checking stories fits the tester.

A.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group needs a tester who can check whether the new repairs service is delivering its intended results. Which person is best suited to the role?
options: Ellen Price, who configures the tenant portal
Kyle Morgan, an informal leader in the contact centre
Deborah Kiely, head of tenant engagement
Amara Okeke, who measures service performance
A.why: Testers make sure products meet their quality and acceptance criteria and deliver value to users. An analyst who measures performance and impact fits the tester role (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: Configuring the portal is building the product: a developer.
whyNot.1: Kyle is an informal leader and key influencer among the advisers.
whyNot.2: Deborah understands tenants' needs across the service and fits the CPO role.

B.q: At Draycott, Hannah Reece, the data science lead, will design and build the machine learning model that predicts machine failures. Which role does she best fit?
options: Tester
Product owner
Developer
Team coach
B.why: Developers design, build and maintain increments of the product and resolve technical issues (Table 7.2). Building the prediction model is development work.

whyNot.0: Testers check products against criteria and the DoD; Hannah builds the model.
whyNot.1: The PO owns the team's backlog and user stories; nothing suggests Hannah does.
whyNot.3: The team coach facilitates and coaches the team; Hannah is a builder.

B.q: At Pinewick, the e-commerce team's backlog must stay aligned with the project backlog, continued business justification and the project tolerances. Which role prepares and maintains the e-commerce team's user stories?
options: Chief product owner
Product owner
Project manager
Team coach
B.why: The PO prepares and maintains the product backlog and user stories, keeping them aligned with the project backlog, continued business justification and tolerances (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: The CPO owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams, not one team's stories.
whyNot.2: The PM consults POs on product backlogs but does not maintain them.
whyNot.3: The team coach can help write stories, but the PO owns and maintains the backlog.

B.q: Easterholm's digital team retrospectives have turned into blame sessions, and two team members are in open conflict. Which role should help the team resolve this?
options: Agile coach
Project manager
Project support
Team coach
B.why: The team coach works closely with the team, builds trust and accountability, resolves conflicts, improves communication and facilitates team workshops such as retrospectives (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: The agile coach works at organization level on systemic blockers, not inside one team.
whyNot.1: The PM is a servant leader for the project; team dynamics are the team coach's focus.
whyNot.2: Project support provides administration, not coaching.

C.q: Callowmere makes Daniel Ferreira, head of the web team, its product owner because he line-manages the developers. Rebecca Lyle, who has managed the team's backlog for two years, joins as a developer. Is this an appropriate application of the guidance for the PO role, and why?
options: Yes, because the PO has direct authority over team members
Yes, because a head of team is a version of the team manager
No, because Rebecca's backlog work fits the PO role better
No, because the PO should come from the supplier, Northmere
C.why: The PO prepares and maintains the product backlog and user stories (Table 7.2). Rebecca has done exactly this for two years, so she is the better fit.

whyNot.0: True of the PO role, but it does not make the line manager the best person for it.
whyNot.1: The PO is a version of the team manager role, but being head of a department does not make someone the PO.
whyNot.3: There is no such rule; each team's PO can come from either side.

C.q: At Draycott, product owner Leanne Park asks Tomasz Zielinski, the team coach, to help engineers write user stories and to facilitate the team planning and team retrospective workshops. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because the team coach helps with stories and workshops
Yes, because the team coach owns the team's product backlog
No, because the product owner should run the team workshops
No, because the agile coach facilitates the team workshops
C.why: The team coach assists with writing user stories and facilitates team workshops (Table 7.2).

whyNot.1: The PO owns the product backlog; the coach helps with it.
whyNot.2: Facilitating team workshops is a team coach duty.
whyNot.3: The agile coach works at organization level, not inside team workshops.

C.q: To keep Larkspur's app team velocity steady, the tester accepts stories as done when developers say they are almost finished, planning to test the rest next sprint. Is this an appropriate application of the tester role, and why?
options: Yes, because velocity forecasts should stay stable
Yes, because testers may automate the tests later
No, because the product owner should test every story
No, because stories are checked against criteria and DoD
C.why: Testers review products against acceptance or quality criteria and the team DoD (Table 7.2). An item is done or not done; there is no 'almost done' (9.3.2.2).

whyNot.0: Stable velocity is useful, but counting unfinished work makes the forecast misleading.
whyNot.1: Testers may automate tests, but that does not make unfinished stories done.
whyNot.2: Testing is the tester's role; the PO does not test every story.

reteach.title: A newsroom team
reteach.question: In a newsroom desk, who decides the story list, who coaches the desk, who writes and who checks?

blocks.body: The desk editor keeps the list of stories in priority order and agrees the day's work with the managing editor: the product owner. The writing coach helps the desk work well together and runs its review meetings: the team coach. Reporters write the stories: developers. Sub-editors check every story against the style guide and facts before it is published: testers.

head: Newsroom
Role
rows: Desk editor with the story list

blocks.text: The editor-in-chief who sets priorities across all desks is the CPO, not a desk's PO.

explain.body: A version of the team manager. Owns the product backlog and user stories, agrees work package descriptions with the PM, delivers within tolerances and works closely with the CPO.

test.q: Pinewick's store operations team needs a product owner. Which person is best suited to the role?
options: Sophie Draper, seconded to lead the team
Bill Rowntree, head of store operations
Fran Okonedo, the e-commerce Scrum master
Gwen Tallowby, retail operations director
test.why: Sophie leads the store operations team's work day to day, which fits the PO role for that team (Table 7.2).

whyNot.1: Bill manages area managers and store standards across the business, not one team's backlog.
whyNot.2: A Scrum master fits the team coach role, and Fran works with the other team.
whyNot.3: Gwen received the mandate: the project executive.

explain.body: Works with one or two teams on self-management, trust, conflict and communication; facilitates team workshops; helps write user stories; a Scrum master fits.

test.q: Which person at Easterholm County Council is best suited to be team coach for the digital team?
options: Gita Bhatt, who led agile adoption in two councils
Helen Crowther, who manages the digital team
Oliver Grant, who runs sprint planning and retros
Amy Fletcher, a senior user researcher
test.why: Oliver facilitates the team's planning and retrospectives, the core of the team coach role (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: Leading adoption across organizations fits the agile coach.
whyNot.1: Line-managing the team is not the team coach role.
whyNot.3: User research is delivery work within the team.

explain.body: Designs, builds and maintains increments of the product, contributes to design, collaborates on technical feasibility and resolves technical issues.

test.q: At Saltmarsh, Ellen Price configures the tenant portal and the text messaging service. Which role does she best fit?
options: Tester
Developer
Product owner
Project support
test.why: Configuring the portal and messaging builds the product increments: developer work (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: Testers check products against criteria; Ellen builds them.
whyNot.2: Nothing suggests she owns the backlog.
whyNot.3: Project support provides administration, not product building.

explain.body: Designs, executes and possibly automates tests and quality reviews; builds quality assurance into iterations; reviews products against acceptance or quality criteria and the team DoD.

test.q: Which activity fits a tester in Callowmere's web team?
options: Prioritizing the team's product backlog
Facilitating the team's retrospective
Building the hub's booking screens
Checking stories against the team DoD
test.why: Testers review products against acceptance or quality criteria and the team DoD (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: Prioritizing the product backlog is the PO's job.
whyNot.1: Facilitating retrospectives is the team coach's job.
